A tilted shelf of grey slabs leans hard toward the camera, every joint and seam in the rock packed tight with flowers growing flat and dense no higher than the loose stones beside them, the bare stone between them slick and wide and going nowhere.

A bowl floored with loose sliding gravel holds flowers only where the stone has finally stopped moving, small tight clumps gripping the settled edges while the fresh grey centre is bare and still shifting underfoot.

A bench of dense short turf runs straight across and ends hard against a wall of bare rock rising out of the right side of the frame, no gradual meeting, just green clump pressed against blank grey stone.

A gully side drops steeply and a tongue of old grey-white snow lies down its centre, still thick and dirty at the edges, while flowers grow in dense low clumps up both sides of it, hemming the snow in tight.

A shoulder scoured almost clean by the wind carries bare pale rock across most of its width, and flowers grow only in the narrow lee stripe sheltered behind each jutting rock, pressed flat and close, nowhere else.

A hollow in the stone has filled with meltwater spread out flat and bright over white gravel, perfectly shallow, the flowers growing in dense short clumps right to where the water begins and their stems reflected broken in it.

Flat pavement-like rock cracked into a deep irregular grid covers the whole near ground, the stone slabs themselves bare and smooth and wide, the flowers crammed into every crack in dense low tufts that follow the grid exactly.

A slope of broken plates of rock lies at a shallow angle, the plates loose enough to clink and shift, flowers threading up through every gap between them in short stiff clumps while the stone surface itself stays clean and grey.

A single bright green strip of flowers follows a buried water seep straight across the picture from one edge to the other, the wet dark line cutting cleanly through wide bare grey stone on both sides of it.

A stream has undercut its bank on the near side, exposing a clean section of dark soil threaded through with roots hanging in mid-air, and the flowers growing along the top lean out over the cut edge in dense low clusters.

A boulder field of house-sized blocks fills the near ground completely, the block faces bare and pale and lichened, the shaded gaps between them floored with dark grit where flowers grow in low dense patches just out of the full glare.

A fan of fine grit spread out below a rock chute covers the middle of the frame, the newest grit at the top still raw and bare, the older grit at the wide lower edge already holding small tight clumps of flowers pressing close to the ground.

A flat rock ledge holds a shallow pool on its flat top, the water perfectly still and showing the sky in it, and flowers grow in dense short clumps along the dry lip of the ledge on all three visible sides of the pool.

A melting snow sheet still covers half the near ground, its surface grey-white and granular and wet, and where its edge is pulling back the dark wet soil is bare for a hand-width before the flowers begin growing close and low.

A rib of pale quartzite runs directly across the picture from the left edge to the right, both ends out of frame, flowers banked in dense clumps against its sunny face and the stone itself bare and bright on top.

A broad hollow of shattered dark rock sits nearly level, the broken pieces angular and loose, and flowers grow only where two or three pieces have locked against each other and stopped moving, in scattered islands across the wreckage.

A bench of old compressed snow, still thick enough to walk on, interrupts the flower ground midway across the frame, flowers growing right to its hard lower edge on both sides while the snow surface stays bare and slightly blue.

A steep bank of loose pale schist drops to a narrow thread of clear water running fast over flat stones, the flowers growing in dense low clumps across the upper bank while the stone near the water is bare and wet and dark.

A shelf of dark basalt tilts sharply forward toward the camera, the surface broken into rough ledges, meltwater running in a thin bright sheet across one ledge and flowers growing in tight low patches between the dry ledges above it.

A wide area of flat grey limestone carries a scatter of loose angular fragments across its surface, and the flowers grow only between the fragments, pressing low into whatever soil has gathered there, the bare stone between them clean and pale.

A seep of water has spread into a wide wet patch of dark grit across the lower frame, and flowers grow in a thick dense band just above where the wet begins, their stems leaning slightly outward over the saturated ground below.

A half-buried slab of granite tilts up out of the slope at a steep angle and flowers grow banked against its uphill face in dense low clumps while the downhill side of the slab is bare stone falling away to loose rubble.

A long bench of compacted old snow curves across the near ground, its upper surface dirty with wind-blown grit, flowers growing right to its far edge where the snow has rotted through and dark wet gravel shows in widening gaps.

A shallow depression lined with small flat stones holds a thin glaze of meltwater over its whole floor, the stones magnified and bright below it, flowers growing in dense short clumps around the outer dry rim of the depression on all sides.

A tall face of bare rock drops straight across the picture, its surface rounded and knobbled where water has worked it, and at its base a narrow band of fine rubble carries flowers growing in dense low clumps.
